correct.title: Correct to
transpose.title: Transpose (semitones)
transpose.shiftNote: {n} semitones ({cents} ¢) — the detected reference doesn't change, only the pitch.
transpose.warning: Large pitch jumps can introduce audible artifacts, especially in vocals and percussion.
howItMeasures.p1: The detector scans the track taking audio windows spread across its full duration. Each window gets an FFT with a Hann window, and each spectral peak's frequency is refined with parabolic interpolation, reaching resolution well below a single bin's width.
howItMeasures.p2: Each peak is compared against the nearest note on the A = 440 Hz tempered scale, and its deviation in cents (modulo 100, with circular math) feeds an energy-weighted histogram. The histogram's peak, refined with a circular mean, gives the global offset; the reference pitch is 440 × 2^(offset/1200). This method is key-independent and doesn't require separating instruments.
howItMeasures.p3: Tonal consistency (R) shows how concentrated the histogram is, but it has a physical ceiling: even a perfectly tuned solo piano gives R≈20-25% due to the natural inharmonicity of its strings, and vibrato widens the histogram for vocal or bowed-string material without the tuning being wrong. That's why low R doesn't mean an ambiguous measurement, and the color thresholds reflect that real ceiling instead of a synthetic-tone ideal.
howItMeasures.p3b: Uncertainty (±) is the honest measure of precision: it's computed by measuring two independent subsets of windows separately (interleaved across the track) and reporting how much they differ. If both halves agree, the measurement is repeatable even when R is low; if they differ, it's the material's tuning that moves across the track, and the verdict says so with the number in plain sight. The drift panel splits the track into segments and estimates each one's reference pitch.
howItMeasures.p4: Correction uses Rubber Band (Finer mode, highest quality) to change pitch without touching tempo. Measuring and correcting always run on the same decode of the file — never measured one way and corrected another.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: Your audio never leaves your device. Centrail has no server, no accounts, and collects no personal data.
privacy.local.title: Where your audio is processed
privacy.local.body: All analysis and all correction happen inside your browser, on your own machine. The file you open is never uploaded: it's read into memory, measured, corrected, and the result is downloaded locally. That's why speed depends on your machine, and why you can work without a connection.
privacy.mic.title: The microphone
privacy.mic.body: The live tuner asks for microphone permission only when you activate it with a click, never automatically. The sound is analysed on the spot to estimate pitch and discarded right away: it isn't recorded, stored or transmitted. When you stop the microphone, the capture closes.
privacy.network.title: The only thing that does leave your device
privacy.network.body: To open the app, your browser downloads it from GitHub Pages, where it's hosted. Those requests are the same ones any website makes: GitHub, like any server, may log technical connection data such as your IP address and browser type. That happens when the page loads, not while you use it. Once loaded, measuring and correcting generate no further requests; installed as an app, not even that.
privacy.storage.title: What's stored in your browser
privacy.storage.body: Centrail remembers two preferences in your browser's local storage: the language you chose and the reference pitch you work with. They stay on your device, they don't travel anywhere, and they disappear if you clear the site's data.
privacy.nothing.title: What there isn't
privacy.nothing.body: No accounts, no sign-up. No third-party analytics, no tracking cookies. No advertising. No data is sold or shared, because none is collected. The code is open and auditable: you can check exactly what it does.
privacy.contact.title: Contact
privacy.contact.body: If you have questions about this policy, you can reach us by opening an issue in the project repository.
